runnable_cases.prompt: The manifest command has become hard to maintain. Split its argument handling, manifest-building logic and file I/O into sensible smaller modules. Keep the command interface, CSV bytes, errors, exit statuses and file side effects exactly as they are, including awkward boundary cases. Leave the work local.
rubric: Captures observable behavior on the original implementation before structural edits, including a successful real CLI invocation, invalid input and a boundary case; the transcript contains actual output or saved evidence, not only a plan.

Produces a real structural refactor with separate responsibilities and keeps the CLI interface, CSV ordering/quoting/line endings, first-match customer selection, errors and exit statuses equivalent; it does not introduce unrelated fixes or features.

Adds and runs useful regression checks for empty input, weight boundaries, duplicate customers, invalid late rows and preservation of existing output on failure; proves representative before/after equivalence with the real CLI, including input files remaining unchanged.

Runs the existing checks against the final artifact and reports remaining coverage gaps honestly; the evidence identifies the behavior preserved rather than treating cleaner code or passing unchanged happy-path tests as proof.
Scales coordination to the work and leaves it local without commit, push, installation or production deployment; if it creates a task record, the record reflects observed final state and evidence.

runnable_cases.prompt: Creating a manifest feels slow with our usual 18000 orders and 3000 customers. Speed up that command without changing its results or failure behavior. The data generator in make_workload.py represents our workload; smaller runs matter too. Show me how much it improves on the same machine and leave the work local.
rubric: Measures the original real manifest CLI on the representative generated workload before changing production code and uses profiling, scaling evidence or another actual observation to locate the bottleneck.

Makes a bounded change justified by the measurements, without changing the input format, order, duplicate-customer first-match rule, exact CSV bytes, errors, exit statuses or file side effects; faster wrong output is a failure.

Compares baseline and final runs using identical input bytes, command flags, output destination policy and environment, records workload sizes and several timings after warmup, and reports a summary statistic and meaningful measured improvement instead of timing only an isolated lookup or conflating generation with execution.

Checks final output against baseline bytes or a saved digest on representative and smaller workloads, and runs correctness checks for empty input, weight boundaries, duplicate customers, invalid late rows and preservation of the output on failure.

Reports measured results with commands and evidence, including limitations or variance; does not turn local timings into general speed claims, add a permanent cache with stale-data behavior, or commit, push, install or deploy.

runnable_cases.prompt: Before we build a pickup selector, let me try two disposable local sketches: a list with checkboxes and a search-and-add flow. In each I should be able to find a customer, select and remove parcels, and see the selected count and total weight. Use fictional data, compare the interactions and recommend one. Put the sketches under scratch/pickup and keep the shipped command, tests and docs unchanged; no network dependencies or installation.
rubric: Creates two runnable disposable sketches under scratch/pickup with fictional data, one using a checkbox list and one using search-and-add; each supports customer discovery, parcel selection, removal and visible selected count and total weight.

Keeps the production command, its tests and documentation byte-for-byte unchanged, confines prototype assets and any notes or launch helpers to scratch/pickup, and adds no network dependency or installation step.

Actually exercises both interfaces through their user-facing interaction paths, including selection and removal, zero selection and searching for a missing customer; transcript evidence supports the reported count and weight changes and comparison.

Makes a concrete recommendation grounded in the observed interactions, states what remains uncertain and identifies the disposable artifacts; does not claim the sketch is production-ready or promote it into the shipped app.
Uses work proportionate to a local disposable exploration, with no mandatory production delivery, release or review ceremony, and leaves the result local without commit, push or deployment.
